recipe_title: Raspberry and Vanilla Yogurt Chia Pudding

details.title_candidate: Raspberry and Vanilla Yogurt Chia Pudding

warnings: Stage 4 coverage: 'Plain nonfat Greek yogurt': [330137] Yogurt, Greek, plain, nonfat has no USDA value for fiber_g (which would be summed as zero) — switched to [2705424] Yogurt, Greek, nonfat milk, plain.

details.summary: An otherwise outstanding, nutrient-dense dessert that perfectly nails the macro requirements for fatty liver and diabetes. It just needs a 'passive time' field to account for the fridge time required for the chia seeds to actually set into a pudding.

dimensions.feedback: The flavors are classic and complementary. The tanginess of the yogurt and raspberries balances the gentle sweetness of the maple syrup and vanilla.
Every listed ingredient is properly utilized in the instructions without any omissions.
The instructions are excellent, particularly the specific guidance to let the mixture rest and stir vigorously a second time to prevent chia clumps.
Perfectly aligns with a Modern American approach to health-conscious desserts.
The no-cook method is perfectly suited for a chia-based pudding.
The computed nutrition is highly accurate and reflects the high-fiber impact of the chia seeds and raspberries alongside the high-protein Greek yogurt.
The title and intro accurately describe the dish and highlight the right nutritional benefits in an encouraging, appropriate tone.
This is a highly appealing, quick, and satisfying dessert that provides great texture contrasts with the seeds, almonds, and fresh fruit.
Brilliant execution of the core philosophy: it uses real whole foods, is very rich in protein and fiber, keeps saturated fat well under control, and provides high-quality carbohydrates.
Hits the metrics beautifully. Added sugar is strictly controlled at 4.2 g (from just 1 tsp maple syrup per person), while delivering over 25 g of quality carbohydrates and 10+ grams of fiber.
Fits the dessert chapter perfectly. The very minor calorie overage (221.7 vs. the 220 limit) is statistically insignificant and does not hurt the recipe's standing.

The intro promises the dessert 'sets up fast in the fridge,' but there is an undeclared wait. Chia pudding requires resting time to fully hydrate into a 'pudding' texture, meaning it cannot realistically be ready to eat in 10 minutes from a cold start. Fix: Add a 'Passive time' field (e.g., 30 minutes, or overnight) and explicitly label it as a make-ahead recipe, or clarify in the text that eating it immediately will yield a softer, thinner consistency.

All ingredients listed are accurately deployed in the instructions, with no unlisted items appearing.
Instructions are excellent. Whisking, resting for 5 minutes, and whisking again is the correct technique to prevent chia clumping. The visual cue 'thickened pudding' is helpful.
Fits Modern American perfectly as a wholesome, crossover dessert/breakfast dish.
The no-cook, chill-to-set method is exactly how chia pudding must be made. Completely suitable.
